title: Field of Soma: Movement and Somatic Education with Kirti Verma
description: Clinical Somatics, Tai Chi and Creative Movement with Kirti Verma. Gentle, body-based education for releasing held tension and moving with ease.
text:
Skip to content
FIELD OF SOMA
MOVEMENT AND SOMATIC EDUCATION
Find your way back
into your body.
Through Somatic healing, Tai Chi, and Creative Movement, rediscover the quiet intelligence your body already holds.
Explore the Practices
Book a Consultation
Your body is not a problem to fix. It is a living field of intelligence, capable of its own restoration, its own expression, its own quiet wisdom.
Kirti Verma
An inquiry into somatic education and embodied presence.
LISTENING TO THE SENSING BODY
Gentle neuromuscular repatterning for chronic tension and nervous system ease.
Login
Book Session
Three practices, one field
Each can be learned on its own. Together they cover how a body heals, steadies and expresses itself.
Heal, sense
Clinical Somatics
Slow, attentive movements that retrain the brain’s control of muscles held tight for years. Nothing is forced or stretched. You learn to release the tension yourself, and to keep it released.
For chronic pain, stiffness, and bodies worn down by stress.
About Clinical Somatics
Ground, flow
Tai Chi
A gentle internal martial art, practised as moving meditation. Weight settles into the legs, the spine lengthens, and the breath follows a slow, circular form. Balance arrives without bracing.
For steadiness, quiet strength and focus.
About Tai Chi
Express, play
Creative Movement
Open movement inquiry drawn from dance. There is no choreography and nothing to perform. You follow sensation, rhythm and curiosity, and let the body say what it has been holding.
For feeling alive, expressive and unguarded in your own skin.
About Creative Movement
THE CONVERGENCE
How three practices become one field
These are not three separate exercises done in sequence. They are three angles on the same living nervous system.

THE CONFLUENCE
Field of Soma
Where healing meets rooting meets play. A single evolving practice where your body can heal, ground and express itself all at once.
SOMATIC PERSPECTIVE
“Most teachers specialize in one. Kirti teaches the three side by side because a body that is only quiet may lack expression, and a body that only dances may carry unaddressed pain.”
Explore the three practices
WHY SOMATICS
Tension you can no longer feel is tension you cannot release.
Years of stress, sitting, injury and guarding teach muscles to stay switched on. In time the brain stops registering them at all. Thomas Hanna named this sensory-motor amnesia.
